source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: a mechanism-level review
finding: Reviews 10 historical architectures, 8 agent runtime families and 42 modern systems. Codes each mechanism by evidence relation (E1-E4) and migration depth (D0-D4). Claims modern agents copied much of the memory, planning and reflection substrate, but adaptive control is uneven.
numbers: 10 architectures, 8 runtime families, 42 systems. Depth scale: D0 concept, D1 interface, D2 explicit state, D3 trigger runs the control transition, D4 outcomes update future control policy.
quote: Memory, planning, reflection, and tool use are often compared as feature labels, obscuring the control semantics
limits: Preprint (Jul 2026). Authors state no inter-rater reliability; D3/D4 scores are provisional and one-coder. Reported score is the highest-depth instance found, not a prevalence.
agent_relevance: Gives a vocabulary to audit our schema: for each state or operator ask what triggers it and whether outcomes change later control.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: a mechanism-level review
finding: Names five residual gaps where old architectures still specify couplings that agents lack: activation with latency and action utility; typed impasse with isolated substate and resolution compilation; bounded content competition with broadcast; persistent intention with reconsideration; uncertainty with resource allocation and stopping.
numbers: 5 residual bundles. One candidate gap (B5, skill routing) was closed by closest-baseline screening because GraSP already combines it.
limits: Gaps are proposals; none is tested by experiment in the paper. The screening search is the authors' own.
agent_relevance: Our schema has impasse-like triggers (G1) but no isolated substate or compiled result; this paper marks that as the open coupling.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: a mechanism-level review
finding: Soar chain is failure type, then scoped recovery, then reusable control knowledge. Retry or reflection captures only a fragment without the typed parent-child state and the compile step. PALADIN, AgentDebugX, Shepherd, Reflexion and AgentHER each cover a piece in separate implementations.
numbers: Pieces rated E3/D4 across separate systems; the full chain (typed impasse, protected substate, typed return, compile) rated residual.
quote: Retry or reflection captures only a fragment when it lacks the typed parent-child state and compilation edge.
limits: A generated recovery can mutate state before diagnosis is validated; a lesson may lack applicability conditions. Argument, not measured.
agent_relevance: Supports G2 (revise only from real output) and suggests storing lessons with explicit applicability conditions.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: a mechanism-level review
finding: ACT-R maps to adaptive memory: activation sets retrieval accessibility and latency, production utility sets action value. AgeMem, Memory-R1, MemCon, DeltaMem, A-MAC and CURATOR learn memory policies from outcomes. Missing is one law joining access time, memory value and action utility.
numbers: Rated E3/D4 for experience-dependent memory control.
limits: Mapping is interpretive. Memory papers measure retrieval and task success, not cross-component invariants.
agent_relevance: Do not add a memory-policy learner (section 4b). If memory is added, gate it on measured payoff at equal tokens (G7).

source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: a mechanism-level review
finding: Three limits on migration. Runtimes split state, tools and memory over separate interfaces, so couplings break. LLM-written summaries and reflections have unstable meaning, unlike typed chunks. Evaluation rewards local capability, not cross-component invariants. The D2-to-D3 gap is mostly an authority gap, not a representation gap.
quote: The gap between D2 and D3 is frequently an authority gap rather than a representation gap.
limits: Authors' judgement.
agent_relevance: Matches our rule that the program, not the model, holds authority over transitions (section 1).

source: Sumers, Yao, Narasimhan, Griffiths (2024) Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (CoALA), TMLR
finding: Proposes CoALA: modular memory (working, episodic, semantic, procedural), a structured action space and a decision cycle. Treats an LLM as a probabilistic production system. Surveys ReAct, Reflexion, Generative Agents, Voyager, ToT and others against this frame.
numbers: Action space has 4 kinds: grounding (external), retrieval, reasoning, learning (internal). Decision cycle = planning (propose, evaluate, select) then execution.
limits: Conceptual framework with no experiments of its own.
agent_relevance: Design check: each of our S-states and O-operators should map to one CoALA action type.

source: Sumers et al. (2024) CoALA, Soar description
finding: Describes Soar for an AI audience: rules propose, evaluate and execute operators; if no action is valid or several tie, an impasse creates a subgoal, giving hierarchical decomposition. Chunking and Soar-RL are named as learning modes.
quote: If no actions are valid, or multiple actions tie, then an impasse occurs. Soar creates a subgoal to resolve the impasse
limits: CoALA's own decision cycle drops the impasse-subgoal step: planning is fixed code with no automatic subgoal on tie or no-change.
agent_relevance: Our impasse detector (G1) is the piece CoALA leaves out; keep it in code.

source: Sumers et al. (2024) CoALA, decision making
finding: Planning has three sub-stages: proposal, evaluation, selection. Evaluation may use heuristics, LLM values, learned values or LLM votes. Learning is a deliberate action chosen in the cycle like any other, not a background process.
limits: Describes a design space; no measured comparison of evaluation methods.
agent_relevance: Maps onto our fill-slot model: model proposes, code evaluates and selects (G5).

source: Sumers et al. (2024) CoALA, memory write risk
finding: Procedural-memory writes are flagged as significantly riskier than episodic or semantic writes, since they can add bugs or let an agent subvert designer intent.
limits: Stated as reasoning, not measured.
agent_relevance: Supports not letting the model rewrite its own schema or operators.

source: Laird (2022) Introduction to the Soar Cognitive Architecture
finding: Soar decision cycle: elaboration, operator proposal, selection by preferences, application. Three impasse types: state no-change, operator tie/conflict, operator no-change. An impasse makes a substate that holds local reasoning; results return to the superstate; substates can nest.
limits: Overview by the architecture's developer, version 9.6; mainly AI-agent description, not human data.
agent_relevance: Gives the exact trigger taxonomy for our impasse detector: no candidate, tie or conflict, stuck.

source: Laird (2022) Introduction to Soar, chunking
finding: Chunking runs automatically whenever a substate creates a result. It traces which superstate structures the result depended on and writes a rule. It turns slow sequential reasoning into parallel rule firing. Author says overhead is minimal and gains outweigh costs.
numbers: No figures given; points to Assanie (2022), not opened.
quote: chunking is a learning mechanism that converts deliberate, sequential reasoning into parallel rule firings
limits: Strong claim made by the developer and not tested in this document.
agent_relevance: LLM analogue: cache a verified solution with its conditions. Only safe if conditions are checked in code.

source: Laird (2022) Introduction to Soar, scope
finding: States the Soar hypothesis: enough regularities exist above the neural level to capture mind functions, so knowledge is mostly symbolic with numeric metadata biasing retrieval and learning. Notes that similarities among Soar, ACT-R and Sigma led to a Common Model of Cognition.
limits: Position statement.
agent_relevance: Supports splitting symbolic control (code) from fuzzy content (model).

source: Yao et al. (2022) ReAct: synergizing reasoning and acting
finding: Interleaving thought and action beats action-only on ALFWorld and WebShop. On HotpotQA and FEVER, plain ReAct is not best: it trails CoT self-consistency on HotpotQA, and a hybrid of the two does better.
numbers: ALFWorld best trial 71% vs Act 45% vs BUTLER 37%; worst ReAct trial 48%; relative gain over Act 33-90%, avg 62% over 6 trials. WebShop +10% absolute. HotpotQA EM (PaLM-540B): Act 25.7, ReAct 27.4, CoT-SC 33.4. FEVER acc: Act 58.9, ReAct 60.9, CoT-SC->ReAct 64.6.
limits: Few-shot prompted PaLM-540B. Table values read from PDF text with garbled layout; check before citing.
agent_relevance: Gains came from tasks needing state tracking, not knowledge QA. ReAct is an operator loop with no commitment step (Wray 2025).

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: Verbal reflection stored in episodic memory improves later trials. Strong on code with unit tests (HumanEval 0.80 to 0.91). Fails to help on MBPP Python (0.80 to 0.77).
numbers: HumanEval Py 0.80->0.91; MBPP Py 0.80->0.77; HumanEval Rust 0.60->0.68; MBPP Rust 0.71->0.75. Test false-positive rate MBPP Py 0.16 vs HumanEval Py 0.01. Authors report +22% AlfWorld, +20% HotPotQA, +11% HumanEval over baselines.
limits: Gain depends on a trustworthy external check. A test that passes a wrong solution misleads the reflection. Self-reported benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for G2 and G3: reflection works when the check is reliable and fails when tests pass wrong solutions.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents
finding: Memory stream, reflection and planning. Ablating each component lowers human-rated believability. Retrieval scores recency, importance and relevance, a rough activation-style rule.
numbers: TrueSkill mu: full 29.89; no reflection 26.88; no reflection or planning 25.64; crowdworker 22.95; no memory/planning/reflection 21.21. 100 evaluators. Full vs prior-work condition d=8.16.
limits: Outcome is believability ranked by raters, not task success. Agents embellish memories.
agent_relevance: Memory plus reflection adds value for persona tasks; it does not show value for problem solving.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager
finding: Skill library of executable code (procedural memory), automatic curriculum and iterative prompting in Minecraft. Beats ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT.
numbers: 63 unique items in 160 iterations, 3.3x others; wooden tool 15.3x, stone 8.5x, iron 6.4x faster; only agent to reach diamond; map distance 2.3x.
limits: GPT-4 and a game API with cheap checks.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM version of chunking: verified code is stored and reused. Needs a cheap executable check.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Search over thoughts (propose, evaluate, backtrack) lifts Game of 24 far above chain of thought. In CoALA terms it is an agent with only reasoning actions and a search decision procedure.
numbers: Game of 24: GPT-4 CoT 4% vs ToT 74%.
limits: Many more calls than plain CoT. Evaluation is by the same model that generates.
agent_relevance: Search needs a program driving it; supports a code-run decision cycle.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT
finding: OS-style memory tiers (main context vs archival and recall storage) with the model issuing function calls to move data. Large gain on deep memory retrieval.
limits: Authors built the DMR task. The model itself decides paging, so paging errors are not code-checked.
agent_relevance: Outside memory helps when the stored fact is needed; the paging decision is a model judgement, against our rule.

source: Wei et al. (2022) Chain-of-thought prompting
finding: Eight CoT exemplars with PaLM 540B reached state of the art on GSM8K. In CoALA terms CoT is a reasoning action that writes into working memory.
quote: PaLM 540B with just eight chain-of-thought exemplars achieves state-of-the-art
limits: Gains appear at large scale.
agent_relevance: Baseline for equal-token comparison (G7).

source: Kirk, Wray, Laird (2023) Exploiting Language Models as a Source of Knowledge for Cognitive Agents
finding: Treat the LLM as a knowledge source the architecture queries and then checks with agent knowledge (parsing, prompting, refine and re-prompt). Raw LLM answers are often unusable for an embodied agent.
numbers: In one task-learning example over 70% of LLM responses were not viable for the embodied agent.
limits: Human-classified single case study; no benchmark numbers.
agent_relevance: Supports verify-before-use: code checks LLM output before it enters state.

source: Zhu & Simmons (2024) Bootstrapping Cognitive Agents with a Large Language Model
finding: Production-rule agent with a task stack (ACT-R goal module, Soar impasse as inspiration). When no production applies it asks the LLM for an action and a new rule. Learned rules then run without the LLM.
numbers: Kitchen tasks, 15 instances each: find 14/15 action-only vs 15/15 bootstrapped; steps not significantly different (p=0.446 find, 0.347 slice). Test cost about $120 for baseline vs under $40 for bootstrapping.
limits: Small kitchen simulator, hand-built production classes, 15 trials per cell. Per-row token counts not copied because the table text was garbled.
agent_relevance: A working impasse-then-compile loop with the LLM as knowledge source; cost falls because rules replace calls.

source: Wray, Kirk, Laird (2025) Applying Cognitive Design Patterns to General LLM Agents
finding: Maps cognitive design patterns (observe-decide-act, commitment and reconsideration, memory, knowledge compilation) onto agentic LLM systems. Says ReAct lacks an explicit commitment step and asks whether adding it helps.
quote: Would introducing commitment in ReAct result in better overall reasoning outcomes than ReAct alone?
limits: Position paper; no experiment. Authors come from the Soar group.
agent_relevance: A testable question for us: does a commit/reconsider step win at equal tokens?

source: Wray, Kirk, Laird (2025) Cognitive Design Patterns, knowledge compilation
finding: ACT-R production compilation and Soar chunking cache reasoning so costly search is not repeated. Agentic LLMs do more search per query, so compilation matters more, but quality and reliability issues remain.
limits: Argument only.
agent_relevance: Same point as G7: pay for any cache or memory by showing equal-token gains.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) review, coding limits
finding: Authors admit the mapping is interpretive: shared nouns, similar diagrams or similar outputs do not count; coding used two passes by the same authors with no second coder.
limits: Independent recoding is promised, not done.
agent_relevance: Treat the E/D codes as hypotheses when we cite the mapping.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) review, skill reuse
finding: Failure-driven learning (Reflexion, AgentHER) changes later behaviour but without typed impasse or conditions of reuse. Voyager, AWM and SGDR are listed as workflow-induction and skill-reuse cases at D4.
limits: One-coder classification.
agent_relevance: Skill reuse is the best-supported LLM counterpart of chunking.

source: Newell (1990) Unified Theories of Cognition
finding: Founding claim cited by Laird 2022 and CoALA: one architecture should embody a unified theory of cognition; Soar was built to test it. Known only through those citations.
limits: Not opened; claim taken only from Laird 2022.
agent_relevance: Context only.

source: Laird, Rosenbloom, Newell (1986) Chunking in Soar: anatomy of a general learning mechanism
finding: Original chunking paper, cited in the CoALA reference list. Not read.
limits: Not opened; no founding numbers recorded.
agent_relevance: Needs a later pass.

source: Anderson et al. (2004) An integrated theory of the mind (ACT-R)
finding: Original ACT-R paper, cited by Wray 2025 and the 2026 review. Not read; the PDF fetch failed and the web search budget ran out.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Needs a later pass for the activation equation and fit numbers.
